title: The Moon's Big Secret
markdown:
Sunrise. Gold light spilled across Noah’s bedroom floor. Birds chirped from the ancient oak. Yet Noah, usually first to dash out, was not leaping. A question had sat on him all night. Last night the moon had hung like a perfect round disc. The night before: a sliver, a tiny thin curve, a shy smile. What was happening?

“It’s a moon-shape mystery!” He bounded from the blankets, pulled on striped pyjamas, and zipped to the garden gate.

Maple the hare was already thumping, dewdrops like tiny diamonds on the grass, each one holding a miniature sun. “Noah! The moon was there — a big bright thing — and then it wasn’t all there! A midnight misunderstanding! Moon confusion!”

Noah’s hair flopped. “Someone is playing tricks. A giant eraser.”

They zipped across the dewy lawn toward Auntie Jo’s cottage. Baking bread. Damp soil. Jo, flour on her hands, apron smudged, tending bright red poppies whose petals unfurled like dancers.

“Auntie Jo! The moon keeps changing shape! Dark ink? Or… eating it at night?”

Maple squeaked. “Everything in the world should stay put. Order is important.”

Jo chuckled, a warm rumble, a happy-cat purr. “Oh, my little investigators. The moon isn’t changing its shape. It’s always perfectly round. A sphere.” She picked up a bright bouncy blue ball from the porch, then a tall gleaming desk lamp.

“Imagine this lamp is our Sun. This ball is our Moon.” She switched the lamp on. Warm gold lit one side of the ball. “The Moon doesn’t make its own light. The Sun’s light bounces off it. A giant dull mirror.”

She moved the ball slowly in a wide circle around the lamp. “When only a curved edge catches the glow, we see a sliver. A crescent. The shy smile you saw a few nights ago.”

Noah leaned in. “So it’s not being nibbled by a cosmic mouse?”

“Not at all.” She showed more of the sunlit side. “Half-moon: half lit from where we stand. And when the whole sunlit face points our way, a full circle.”

Maple hopped. “It’s turning? And the sun is showing different bits of its sunny side? Hide-and-seek?”

“A dance above our heads. The Moon stays round. Our view of the sunlit face changes over about a month. That’s why it seems to change shape.”

A thrill went through Noah. Not a trick. A chartable thing. His pencil made bold lines and quick circles. “A full month. Every phase, tiny or grand.”

Maple’s nose twitched. “Official moon observers. No more moon confusion.”

Jo watched them, proud without making a speech of it. “Lunar phases. The predictable dance of Moon and Sun.”

They burst out the garden gate into bright morning, notebook already hungry. Today, Noah declared, was going to be amazing — starting with breakfast, then a sketch of last night’s disc, then whatever shy smile came next. The pancakes, Maple noted, were fully round, and nobody had erased them.
characters: Noah (a weather note-taker), Maple (a hare), Auntie Jo (a cook)
